question: Does the CPU:GPU ratio separate architecture families into a usable prior?
WHY I DO NOT REPORT THE TOOL VERDICT AS: Four of the five families have n=1. The entire within-family spread the rule compares against comes from qwen3's two bodies. A 2x between/within rule is too permissive at this shape, and my own tool is the thing over-claiming.

prefill.reading: Not 'families separate'. ONE family is an outlier: granitemoehybrid at 50.85x against four families clustered in 6.0-10.6x. Drop it and the remaining spread is 65%, comparable to qwen3's 34% WITHIN-family spread. The honest claim is a hybrid-SSM outlier, not a family taxonomy.

decode.reading: 11.63-14.94x, a 25% band across five families, with qwen3's own two bodies spanning 7.8% of it. Between-family 22% against within-family 8% barely clears the 2x rule and rests on one family's within-spread. Consistent with a host constant plus noise; not a usable prior.

operational: Do not use decode ratio as an architecture prior. The prefill outlier is worth one thing only: hybrid SSM prefill is disproportionately GPU-dependent, which is the SAME family whose larger bodies (Jamba2-3B, granite-4.0-h-tiny, Falcon-H1-7B) reproducibly exceed this host's Metal command-buffer watchdog on a 512-token prefill. Two independent measurements pointing at one mechanism.
reopen_when: a second body lands in any family other than qwen3, which is what would make the within-family term real
caveat: 9 CPU rows exist but only 6 bodies have BOTH axes; the rest are refused or owed on gpu.
